question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{2w}-\sqrt{6}} & = \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{2w}-\sqrt{6}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6}} & = \\ \frac{2(\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6})}{(\sqrt{2w}-\sqrt{6})(\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6})} & = \\ \frac{2(\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6})}{(\sqrt{2w})^{2}-(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{2(\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6})}{2w-6} & = \\ \frac{2(\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6})}{2(w-3)} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2w}+\sqrt{6}}{w-3}\end{aligned}
$$
